key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the title 'Desi Boys' does not qualify as a 'literary work' under Section 13 of the Copyright Act, 1957, and therefore, no copyright subsists in it.
witness_credibility: The court did not assess the credibility of the main witnesses as the case primarily revolved around legal interpretation of copyright law rather than witness testimony.
trial_duration: Dates of offence not stated, trial judgment dated 22.03.2012, High Court decision not stated, Supreme Court decision dated OCTOBER 15, 2015
legal_representation: Raju Ramachandran, Chirag M. Shroff, Bhaskar Das, Nitin Mishra, Mrs. Mitali Gupta, Vikram Aditya Narayan, Advs. for the Appellants; Ramsuresh Vishwakarma, Rajiv Kumar Sinha, Dr. (Mrs.) Vipin Gupta, Kunal A. Cheema, Nishant Ramakantrao Katneshwarkar, Ms. Asha Gopalan Nair, Advs., for the Respondents
investigation_status: Process issued under Section 63 of the Copyright Act, 1957 read with Sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860
appeal_history: Trial court: Complaint and process issued; High Court: Refused to quash the complaint and process issued; Supreme Court: Allowed the appeals, quashed the criminal proceedings
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the respondent No.1, Shyam Vithalrao Devkatta, had claimed copyright in the title of the synopsis of a story 'Desi Boys' and that the appellants' film titled 'Desi Boyz' infringed this copyright.
defence_argument: The defence argued that there is no copyright in the title of a story or film, and therefore, the criminal complaint under Section 63 of the Copyright Act is not tenable.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that a title of a work, by itself, is not a subject of copyright and that copyright subsists only in original literary works as defined under Section 13 of the Copyright Act, 1957.
precedent_relied_upon: Francis Day & Hunter Ltd. v. Twentieth Century Fox Corporation Ltd. and Ors. AIR 1940 Privy Council 55; E.M. Forster and Anr. v. A.N. Parasuram AIR 1964 Madras 331; Kanungo Media (P) Ltd. v RGV Film Factory & Ors. (2007) ILR 1 Delhi 1122; R. Radha Krishnan v. Mr. A.R. Murugadoss & Ors. 2013-5-L.W. 429; Hogg v. Maxwell (1866-67) L.R.2 Ch. App. 307; Macmillan v. Suresh Chander Deb ILR 17 Cat 951; Longman v. Winchester (1809)16 Ves 269; Dicks v. Yates (1881) 18 Ch D 79
